questions.scenario: You drop your phone and the screen shatters. What is your first thought about its design?

options.text: Why don't they design phones with built-in, sleek bumpers that look futuristic?
Phones should be built with the shock-absorbing materials they use in car bumpers.
It's so annoying that I can't easily repair this myself and have to create electronic waste.
The phone is too wide for a normal hand anyway, which is why it slipped in the first place.

questions.scenario: You are asked to design a new chair for a school project. What is your priority?

options.text: Embedding a wireless charging pad and hidden LED lights into the armrests.
Making it look fast and streamlined, like the bucket seat of a sports car.
Building it entirely out of recycled cardboard and upcycled plastics.
Making sure it perfectly supports the lower back so students can sit for hours without pain.

questions.scenario: When you look at everyday objects (like a toothbrush or a pen), what annoys you the most?

options.text: When they look outdated and clunky instead of sleek and minimal.
When they look boring and static—I want things to look dynamic and fast.
When they are wrapped in unnecessary layers of single-use plastic packaging.
When the grip actually hurts your fingers after using it for just 10 minutes.

questions.scenario: You have a free afternoon to watch YouTube videos. What are you most likely watching?

options.text: A teardown video showing the complex circuit boards and camera lenses inside the newest smartphone.
A behind-the-scenes look at how designers sculpt massive clay models for new supercars.
A mini-documentary on how scientists are inventing a new type of leather made from mushrooms.
A video explaining the biomechanics of the human hand and why certain controllers feel better to hold.

questions.scenario: If you were given a block of professional modeling clay right now, what would you naturally start shaping?

options.text: A futuristic VR headset or a sleek smart-watch concept.
A streamlined sports car, drone, or a sleek motorcycle.
I'd want to mix the clay with other organic materials to see if I can create a brand new texture.
A custom joystick or handle that molds perfectly to the exact shape of my palm.

questions.scenario: What do you think makes a physical product feel truly 'premium' or expensive?

options.text: Flawless glass or metal finishes, hidden buttons, and seamless technology.
Aggressive styling, carbon fiber details, and high-performance engineering.
The fact that it is 100% biodegradable, ethically sourced, and leaves zero footprint.
The fact that its weight is perfectly balanced and it feels like an extension of your own body.

questions.scenario: Your school asks you to redesign the cafeteria food trays. What is your winning idea?

options.text: Add a snap-in magnetic slot for smartphones so students can easily watch videos while eating.
Give them curved, aerodynamic edges so they slide super fast and smoothly across the counter.
Make them out of compressed bamboo or wheat-straw instead of cheap, brittle plastic.
Change the weight distribution and handles so they don't tip over when carried with one hand.

questions.scenario: Which of these advanced tools sounds the most fun to learn?

options.text: 3D modeling software for rendering photorealistic tech gadgets with glowing lights.
Wind tunnel simulation software for testing aerodynamic drag and speed.
Advanced 3D printers that can print using recycled ocean plastics or algae.
Motion-capture technology that tracks exactly how human muscles move when lifting an object.

questions.scenario: You buy a brand new pair of expensive headphones. What is the very first thing you notice when unboxing them?

options.text: The sleek, matte finish and the invisible touch-controls on the side.
The smooth, sweeping curves that make them look like they belong in a spaceship.
The clever, origami-style cardboard box that doesn't use any plastic wrap or tape.
How the ear cushions perfectly distribute pressure without pinching your glasses or ears.

questions.scenario: If you had to design a completely new type of backpack, what would be its main feature?

options.text: Built-in solar panels, a power bank, and a hardshell casing to protect laptops.
A sleek, tear-drop shape designed specifically to reduce drag while riding a bike or motorcycle.
It's modular—if a strap breaks, you can easily buy just the strap instead of throwing the bag away.
A heavily researched strap system that completely removes all pressure from your shoulders and spine.

Consumer_Electronics_Designer.title: Consumer Electronics Designer
Consumer_Electronics_Designer.primary_match_text: You are obsessed with the future. You love sleek aesthetics, minimalism, and the way technology integrates seamlessly into physical objects.
Consumer_Electronics_Designer.day_in_the_life: Sketching concepts for the next generation of smartwatches, rendering photorealistic 3D models of laptops, and working with engineers to fit massive batteries into paper-thin devices.
Consumer_Electronics_Designer.alternative_match_text: Because you love how humans interact with tech, transitioning into digital UX/UI (User Experience) Design for apps and software is a very natural backup plan.
Consumer_Electronics_Designer.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) or Commerce/Humanities with Math in 11th/12th. Pursue a Bachelor of Design (B.Des) in Industrial Design or Product Design, focusing on consumer tech.

Automotive_Concept_Designer.title: Automotive / Transportation Designer
Automotive_Concept_Designer.primary_match_text: You are drawn to speed, curves, and dynamic forms. You see products not just as tools, but as high-performance machines that look like they are moving even when standing still.
Automotive_Concept_Designer.day_in_the_life: Sculpting 1:4 scale models of futuristic electric vehicles out of industrial clay, testing aerodynamic drag in digital wind tunnels, and sketching hypercars.
Automotive_Concept_Designer.alternative_match_text: Since you love designing complex, moving machinery, a career in Mechanical Engineering or Aerospace Design would perfectly match your need for high-performance engineering.
Automotive_Concept_Designer.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Des in Transportation Design or Automobile Design. Sketching vehicles daily is crucial for your portfolio.

Sustainable_Product_Designer.title: Sustainable Materials / Circular Designer
Sustainable_Product_Designer.primary_match_text: You are a problem solver for the planet. You care deeply about how things are made, what happens when they break, and how clever design can eliminate waste completely.
Sustainable_Product_Designer.day_in_the_life: Researching bio-plastics made from algae, designing modular shoes that can be easily repaired, and creating clever zero-waste packaging for global brands.
Sustainable_Product_Designer.alternative_match_text: With your passion for the environment and smart materials, working in Environmental Engineering or Sustainable Packaging Strategy is a high-impact alternative.
Sustainable_Product_Designer.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th (Science preferred for material studies). Pursue a B.Des in Industrial Design, specializing in Sustainable Design or Material Futures.

Human_Factors_Ergonomics_Designer.title: Human Factors / Ergonomics Designer
Human_Factors_Ergonomics_Designer.primary_match_text: You are deeply empathetic to the human body. You notice when things are uncomfortable, heavy, or awkward to use, and you naturally want to engineer a physical solution.
Human_Factors_Ergonomics_Designer.day_in_the_life: Studying human anatomy, testing medical devices to ensure they fit perfectly in a surgeon's hand, or designing high-end office chairs that eliminate back pain.
Human_Factors_Ergonomics_Designer.alternative_match_text: If you love understanding the human body and how it moves, a career in Biomechanics, Kinesiology, or even specialized Physiotherapy could be incredibly fulfilling.
Human_Factors_Ergonomics_Designer.roadmap: Take Science (PCB or PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Des in Product Design, followed by a specialization or Master's in Human Factors Engineering or Ergonomics.
